newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk minister says next T-bill auction on Dec 4.
newsitem.headline: Turk minister says next T-bill auction on Dec 4.

text.p: Turkish Treasury will not be issuing any more T-bills until December 4 because of a fall in cash needs, state minister Ufuk Soylemez said on Tuesday.
"The Treasury will not hold auctions until December 4 because it does not have redemption or cash requirements," Soylemez, who is in charge of the Treasury, told Reuters.
"Auctions will be regularly held after December 4 according to redemption dates," he added.
The Treasury, which will repay 135.6 trillion lira of t-bills on Wednesday, will not have redemptions until 154.2 trillion lira of t-bills mature on December 4.

The Treasury auctioned 51.49 trillion lira worth of 182-day bills on Tuesday with Wednesday values at a maximum yield of 144.92 percent, up sharply from 135.16 percent in last week's 182-day bill auction.
It will collect 32.4 trillion lira in auction payments from the banks on Wednesday and repay them 135.6 trillion lira for maturing t-bills.

Soylemez said the Treasury's near-term borrowing requirements would be met through domestic issue of foreign currency-denominated bonds and through a 750 million mark, five-year Eurobond announced earlier on Tuesday.

"The sale of $900 million worth foreign currency-denominated bonds to Turkish banks will be concluded this week, and the Treasury will continue domestic and foreign borrowing in line with market conditions," he said.
Soylemez said last week the forex-denominated bond sales to Turkish banks, which totalled $2 billion since late September, would cover the Treasury's foreign debt servicing until January 1997.
